body.statement: For \(d\geq4\), let \(D_d\in\mathbb R[S_d]\) be nonconstant, homogeneous, and exactly self-normalizing, and let \(G_{D_d}\) denote its trace-pairing symmetric gradient. The all-dimensional rigidity theorem settles every positive-gradient corank-one branch by producing a fixed kernel line and a compression to its orthogonal complement. In the remaining branches, where the relevant positive-semidefinite polynomial gradient has generic rank at most \(d-2\) and hence identically vanishing adjugate, determine whether the self-normalization equations force a recursive common invariant flag, or construct the least-dimensional polynomial counterexample with varying spectral data and certify that no recursive flag represents it.
body.justification: The corank-one kernel step is dimension-free; the first unresolved algebraic branch is now generic rank at most \(d-2\).
body.gap: Tamano's all-dimensional converse assumes a common invariant flag, while the adjugate method becomes identically zero in the remaining higher-corank branch.
body.consumer: A resolution of this narrowed question would determine whether exhaustive reduced-denominator auditing extends beyond three covariance directions.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine whether the self-normalization equations in dimensions at least four force a recursive common invariant flag when the relevant positive-semidefinite polynomial gradient has generic rank at most \(d-2\), or construct and certify a least-dimensional counterexample.
obligation.obstruction: In the remaining branch all \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minors vanish identically, so \(\operatorname{adj}G\equiv0\) and the adjugate translation direction disappears. The first two spectral power sums supplied by homogeneity and self-normalization do not determine a spectrum with four or more entries.
obligation.attempted: The dimension-free adjugate-translation proof and the two-sided cone-order argument close every corank-one case. A direct substitution of lower cofactors was examined, but determinant differentiation does not imply Hessian annihilation in any such lower-cofactor direction.
obligation.partial_result: The all-dimensional rigidity theorem proves that if a relevant polynomial gradient is positive semidefinite on the positive-definite cone, has identically zero determinant, and has rank \(d-1\) at one positive-definite point, then it contains one fixed global kernel line and the polynomial descends to the compression on its orthogonal complement.  If no such point exists, every \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor vanishes identically; hence the generic rank is at most \(d-2\) and \(\operatorname{adj}G\equiv0\).  Thus the corank-one obstruction is closed in every dimension, and only the higher-corank branch remains.
